q: Under Section 10A of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, the parties to an industrial dispute may refer the dispute to arbitration:

options.A: Only after the dispute has been referred for adjudication to a Tribunal
options.B: Only with the permission of the Conciliation Officer appointed for the area
options.C: Voluntarily, by an agreement in writing, at any time before the dispute has been referred to a Labour Court, an Industrial Tribunal or a National Tribunal
options.D: Only where the dispute arises in a public utility service

e: Section 10A of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 allows parties to refer a dispute voluntarily to arbitration by a written agreement at any time before the dispute has been referred to a Labour Court, Industrial Tribunal or National Tribunal.

q: A railway servant who has exhausted the remedies of appeal and revision under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules may submit a memorial to:

options.A: The General Manager of the Railway
options.B: The Railway Board
options.C: The Central Administrative Tribunal
options.D: The President of India

e: After exhausting appeal and revision under the RS (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1968, a railway servant may submit a memorial to the President of India, which is the final departmental remedy of that kind.

q: Under Rule 20 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not:

options.A: Become a member of a recognised service association
options.B: Publish a work of a purely literary or scientific character
options.C: Bring, or attempt to bring, any political or other outside influence to bear upon any superior authority to further his interests in respect of matters pertaining to his service
options.D: Exercise his vote at an election to a local authority

e: Rule 20 of the RS (Conduct) Rules, 1966 prohibits a railway servant from bringing or attempting to bring any political or other outside influence on a superior authority to further his interests in matters pertaining to his service.

q: Under Rule 3C of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966:

options.A: No railway servant shall indulge in any act of sexual harassment of any woman at any workplace
options.B: Sexual harassment at the workplace is punishable only under the criminal law and is not a misconduct under the Conduct Rules
options.C: A complaint of sexual harassment can be made only to the police authorities
options.D: The prohibition applies only in offices where ten or more women are employed

e: Rule 3C of the RS (Conduct) Rules, 1966 expressly provides that no railway servant shall indulge in any act of sexual harassment of any woman at any workplace, making it a misconduct under the Conduct Rules itself.

q: The Permanent Negotiating Machinery for dealing with the grievances and demands of railway employees functions at:

options.A: Three tiers, namely the Railway Board level, the Zonal Railway level and the Divisional level
options.B: Two tiers, namely the Railway Board level and the Zonal Railway level
options.C: The Railway Board level only
options.D: Four tiers, including the workshop level as a separate tier

e: The Permanent Negotiating Machinery for grievances and demands of railway employees functions at three tiers: the Railway Board level, the Zonal Railway level and the Divisional level.

q: Under the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946, the draft standing orders submitted by an employer of an industrial establishment are certified, after following the prescribed procedure, by:

options.A: The Inspector of Factories of the area
options.B: The Labour Commissioner of the State
options.C: The Registrar of Trade Unions
options.D: The Certifying Officer appointed under the Act

e: Under the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946, draft standing orders are certified, after the prescribed procedure of hearing objections, by the Certifying Officer appointed under the Act.

q: In regard to the endorsement of family pension in the Pension Payment Order issued to a retiring railway servant, the correct position is that:

options.A: A separate Pension Payment Order is issued to the spouse only after the death of the pensioner
options.B: Family pension can be sanctioned only through a fresh Pension Payment Order after the death of the pensioner
options.C: The spouse must apply to the Railway Board for sanction of family pension
options.D: The family pension payable to the spouse after the death of the pensioner stands endorsed in the pensioner's own Pension Payment Order

e: Family pension for the spouse is endorsed in the pensioner's own Pension Payment Order at the time of retirement, so on the pensioner's death the endorsed family pension starts on that same PPO without a fresh PPO or fresh sanction.

q: Under Section 7(6) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, where the Central Public Information Officer fails to provide the information within the time specified for the purpose, the information shall be provided to the applicant:

options.A: On payment of double the normal fee
options.B: Only after the disposal of his first appeal
options.C: Free of charge
options.D: Only in the succeeding financial year

e: Section 7(6) of the RTI Act, 2005 provides that where the Central Public Information Officer fails to provide information within the specified time, the information shall be provided free of charge to the applicant.

q: Under Section 6(3) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, where an application for information relates to information held by another public authority, the Central Public Information Officer to whom the application is made shall transfer the application to that other public authority:

options.A: Within thirty days, and need not inform the applicant of the transfer
options.B: Within five days from the receipt of the application, and shall inform the applicant about the transfer immediately
options.C: Within forty-eight hours in all cases
options.D: Only after obtaining the orders of the First Appellate Authority

e: Section 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005 requires the Central Public Information Officer to transfer an application concerning information held by another public authority to that authority within five days of receipt, and to inform the applicant about the transfer immediately.

q: Under Section 22 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, the provisions of the Act:

options.A: Are subordinate to the provisions of the Official Secrets Act, 1923
options.B: Are overridden by the Official Secrets Act, 1923 in case of any inconsistency
options.C: Shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in the Official Secrets Act, 1923 or in any other law for the time being in force
options.D: Have ceased to operate after the repeal of the Freedom of Information Act

e: Section 22 of the RTI Act, 2005 gives the Act overriding effect: its provisions apply notwithstanding anything inconsistent in the Official Secrets Act, 1923 or any other law in force.

q: Two railway servants are transferred on mutual exchange at their own request. In regard to their seniority in the new seniority unit, the correct position is that:

options.A: Both of them are placed at the bottom of the seniority list of the new unit
options.B: Only the senior of the two, with reference to the old unit, retains his seniority in the new unit
options.C: The seniority of each of them in the new unit is determined with reference to his seniority in the old unit, so that they effectively exchange places
options.D: Their seniority in the new unit is determined afresh on the basis of their respective ages

e: On mutual exchange transfer at own request, each railway servant takes the seniority position of the other in the new unit, the seniority of each being determined with reference to his seniority in the old unit, so they effectively exchange places; neither drops automatically to the bottom.

q: Under Section 22 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, in the case of a public utility service such as the Railways, workmen who have given a notice of strike cannot go on strike before the expiry of:

options.A: 14 days from the date on which the notice is given
options.B: 7 days from the date on which the notice is given
options.C: 21 days from the date on which the notice is given
options.D: 30 days from the date on which the notice is given

e: Section 22 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 bars workmen in a public utility service from going on strike within fourteen days of giving the notice of strike, and also bars striking before the date specified in the notice.

q: Under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, 'lock-out' means:

options.A: A cessation of work by a body of workmen acting in combination
options.B: The termination of the services of all the workmen of an establishment
options.C: The permanent closure of an industrial establishment
options.D: The temporary closing of a place of employment, or the suspension of work, or the refusal by an employer to continue to employ any number of persons employed by him

e: Section 2(l) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 defines lock-out as the temporary closing of a place of employment, or suspension of work, or refusal by an employer to continue to employ any number of persons employed by him.

q: Under Section 2(oo) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, 'retrenchment' means:

options.A: The termination by the employer of the service of a workman for any reason whatsoever, otherwise than as a punishment and except in the cases expressly excluded, such as voluntary retirement, superannuation and continued ill-health
options.B: The termination of the service of a workman only on the ground of surplus staff
options.C: The dismissal of a workman only on the ground of misconduct
options.D: The termination of service only on the closure of the establishment

e: Section 2(oo) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 defines retrenchment as termination of a workman's service for any reason whatsoever, otherwise than as punishment, excluding voluntary retirement, superannuation, termination under a fixed-term stipulation and termination due to continued ill-health.

q: Under Section 9C of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, every employer of an industrial establishment is required to set up a Grievance Redressal Committee for the resolution of disputes arising out of individual grievances of workmen, where the number of workmen employed in the establishment is:

options.A: 10 or more
options.B: 50 or more
options.C: 100 or more
options.D: 20 or more

e: Section 9C of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 requires a Grievance Redressal Committee in every industrial establishment employing twenty or more workmen, for resolution of disputes arising out of individual grievances.

q: Under Section 25U of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a person who commits an unfair labour practice is punishable with:

options.A: Fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees only
options.B: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years in all cases
options.C: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both
options.D: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both

e: Section 25U of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 punishes commission of an unfair labour practice with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.

q: Under Section 9 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, an employee shall be disqualified from receiving bonus under the Act if he is dismissed from service for:

options.A: Absence from duty without leave
options.B: Fraud, or riotous or violent behaviour, or theft, misappropriation or sabotage of any property of the establishment
options.C: Habitual late attendance
options.D: Participation in the activities of a registered trade union

e: Section 9 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 disqualifies an employee dismissed from service for fraud, riotous or violent behaviour, or theft, misappropriation or sabotage of any property of the establishment, from receiving bonus.

q: Under the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, the mechanism of 'set-on' and 'set-off' provides that:

options.A: The excess allocable surplus, after payment of the maximum bonus, is carried forward as set-on to the succeeding accounting years, and a deficiency is carried forward as set-off to be made good in the succeeding years
options.B: The entire excess allocable surplus lapses to the employer at the end of the accounting year
options.C: The excess allocable surplus is distributed among the employees as ex-gratia payment
options.D: The excess allocable surplus is credited to the Staff Benefit Fund

e: Under the set-on and set-off mechanism in the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 read with the Fourth Schedule, excess allocable surplus after paying maximum bonus is carried forward as set-on to succeeding years, and a deficiency is carried forward as set-off to be adjusted in succeeding years.

q: The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 applies to:

options.A: Factories and mines only
options.B: Every factory, mine, oilfield, plantation, port and railway company, among others
options.C: Establishments employing one hundred or more employees only
options.D: Public sector undertakings only

e: Section 1(3) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 applies the Act to every factory, mine, oilfield, plantation, port and railway company, among other specified establishments.

q: Under the Railway Services (Pension) Rules, the term 'pension', as defined in the Rules:

options.A: Does not include gratuity in any circumstances
options.B: Includes gratuity, except where the term pension is used in contradistinction to gratuity
options.C: Includes only the monthly pension and not its commuted value
options.D: Includes the Provident Fund accumulations of the railway servant

e: Under the RS (Pension) Rules, the term pension includes gratuity, except where the term pension is used in contradistinction to gratuity in the context of a rule.

q: Under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, where the amount of gratuity payable to an employee is not paid by the employer within the prescribed period of thirty days from the date on which it becomes payable, the employer is liable to pay on the amount:

options.A: No interest in any circumstances
options.B: Compound interest from the date of termination of employment
options.C: Interest only if so directed by a court of law
options.D: Simple interest from the date on which the gratuity becomes payable to the date of actual payment

e: Under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, gratuity unpaid after the prescribed thirty days carries simple interest from the date it becomes payable to the date of actual payment, as provided in Section 7(3A).

q: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where an injury caused to an employee results in his permanent partial disablement, the compensation payable to him is:

options.A: The same as is payable for permanent total disablement in all cases
options.B: One-fourth of the compensation payable for permanent total disablement
options.C: Such percentage of the compensation which would have been payable in the case of permanent total disablement as is proportionate to the loss of earning capacity permanently caused by the injury
options.D: Not payable, as compensation under the Act is admissible only for total disablement

e: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, compensation for permanent partial disablement is such percentage of the compensation payable for permanent total disablement as is proportionate to the loss of earning capacity permanently caused by the injury.

q: Under Section 8 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, where the amount of gratuity due to an employee is not paid by the employer within the prescribed time, it may be recovered from the employer, after it is determined to be payable:

options.A: Only through a civil suit filed by the employee in a court of law
options.B: By adjustment against the Provident Fund balance of the employer
options.C: Only after the employee attains the age of superannuation
options.D: As arrears of land revenue, by the Collector, on the issue of a certificate for that amount by the controlling authority

e: Section 8 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 provides that unpaid gratuity, after determination and issue of a certificate by the controlling authority, is recovered by the Collector as arrears of land revenue.

q: A railway servant who is awarded a Chakra-series gallantry award, such as the Ashok Chakra, is provided under the pass rules with:

options.A: One set of privilege passes every year for a period of five years
options.B: A complimentary card pass entitling him to free travel in AC First Class, along with a companion, for his lifetime
options.C: Duty passes for travel anywhere in India, admissible only after his retirement
options.D: No special pass facility of any kind

e: Under the Railway Pass Rules, a railway servant awarded a Chakra-series gallantry award such as the Ashok Chakra is given a complimentary card pass for free travel in AC First Class with a companion for his lifetime.

q: Under Section 36 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, in any proceeding under the Act, a party to an industrial dispute is entitled to be represented by a legal practitioner:

options.A: In no case whatsoever
options.B: As a matter of right in all cases
options.C: Only with the consent of the other party to the proceeding and the leave of the Conciliation Officer, Labour Court, Tribunal or National Tribunal, as the case may be
options.D: Only where the party is an employer and not where the party is a workman

e: Section 36 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 entitles a party to be represented by a legal practitioner only with the consent of the other party and the leave of the Conciliation Officer, Labour Court, Tribunal or National Tribunal, as the case may be.

q: The Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 applies to every industrial establishment in which:

options.A: 100 or more workmen are employed
options.B: 20 or more workmen are employed
options.C: 50 or more workmen are employed
options.D: 300 or more workmen are employed

e: The Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 applies to every industrial establishment in which 100 or more workmen are employed, subject to State amendments in some States.

q: The Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 applies to every establishment in which:

options.A: Twenty or more workmen are employed, or were employed on any day of the preceding twelve months, as contract labour
options.B: Ten or more workmen are employed as contract labour
options.C: Fifty or more workmen are employed as contract labour
options.D: One hundred or more workmen are employed as contract labour

e: The Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 applies to every establishment in which twenty or more workmen are employed, or were employed on any day of the preceding twelve months, as contract labour.

q: Under Section 13 of the Apprentices Act, 1961, a trade apprentice engaged in an establishment, such as a railway workshop, is entitled, during the period of his apprenticeship training, to:

options.A: The wages payable to a regular skilled workman of the establishment
options.B: No payment of any kind from the establishment
options.C: Only free hostel accommodation in lieu of any payment
options.D: Payment of a stipend at a rate not less than the prescribed rate

e: Section 13 of the Apprentices Act, 1961 entitles a trade apprentice to payment of a stipend during training at a rate not less than the prescribed rate; he is a trainee, not a regular workman on workman wages.

q: Under the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, the minimum rates of wages fixed by the appropriate Government are required to be reviewed, and if necessary revised, at intervals not exceeding:

options.A: Five years
options.B: One year
options.C: Two years
options.D: Ten years

e: Under the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, minimum rates of wages fixed by the appropriate Government must be reviewed, and if necessary revised, at intervals not exceeding five years.

q: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where compensation under the Act is payable in respect of an employee whose injury has resulted in his death, the employer:

options.A: Shall pay the amount of compensation directly to the widow of the deceased employee
options.B: Shall deposit the amount with the Commissioner, and any payment made by the employer to a dependant in discharge of the liability shall not be deemed to be a payment of compensation
options.C: May retain the amount with himself till a claim is filed before a civil court
options.D: Shall credit the amount to the Staff Benefit Fund of the Railway

e: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, compensation for death must be deposited with the Commissioner; a payment made by the employer directly to a dependant in discharge of the liability is not deemed to be a payment of compensation under the Act.

q: Under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, where a contractor fails to make payment of wages to the contract labour engaged by him within the prescribed period, the liability to make the payment in the first instance falls on:

options.A: The Labour Commissioner of the State
options.B: The trade union of the contract labour concerned
options.C: No person, as the contract labour must recover the wages from the contractor alone
options.D: The principal employer, who may recover the amount so paid from the contractor

e: Under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, if the contractor fails to pay wages within the prescribed period, the principal employer must pay the wages and may recover the amount from the contractor.

q: Under Section 4(2) of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, the Internal Complaints Committee shall consist of, among others:

options.A: A Presiding Officer who shall be a woman employed at a senior level at the workplace, and not less than one-half of its total members shall be women
options.B: A Presiding Officer who shall be the senior-most male officer of the workplace
options.C: Members all of whom shall be drawn from outside the establishment
options.D: No member from outside the establishment in any case

e: Section 4(2) of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 requires the Internal Complaints Committee to be headed by a Presiding Officer who is a woman employed at a senior level at the workplace, with not less than one-half of its total members being women and one external member.

q: Where both the husband and the wife are railway servants, House Rent Allowance is admissible:

options.A: To both of them, subject to the fulfilment of the prescribed conditions
options.B: Only to the spouse who is senior in service
options.C: Only to the husband in all cases
options.D: To neither of them

e: House Rent Allowance is admissible to both spouses where both husband and wife are railway servants, subject to fulfilment of the prescribed conditions such as not occupying Government accommodation allotted to either.

q: In regard to the combination of Extra Ordinary Leave with other kinds of leave, the correct position is that:

options.A: Extra Ordinary Leave can never be combined with any other kind of leave
options.B: Extra Ordinary Leave can be granted only after the Leave on Average Pay at credit is fully exhausted and must always stand alone
options.C: Extra Ordinary Leave can be granted only on medical certificate
options.D: Extra Ordinary Leave may be granted in continuation of any other kind of leave admissible to the railway servant

e: Under IREM leave rules, Extra Ordinary Leave may be granted in continuation of, that is in combination with, any other kind of leave admissible to the railway servant; it is not confined to medical grounds or to exhaustion of LAP alone.

q: The interest on the accumulations at the credit of a subscriber to the General Provident Fund is:

options.A: Not payable on the accumulations after the year 2011
options.B: Payable only at the time of the final closure of the account
options.C: Credited to his account annually at the rate determined by the Government from time to time
options.D: Payable at a fixed rate of 12 per cent per annum in perpetuity

e: Interest on General Provident Fund accumulations is credited to the subscriber's account annually at the rate determined by the Government from time to time; it is neither a perpetual fixed 12 per cent nor stopped after 2011.

q: Arrears of pay and allowances due to a railway servant for a past period, which could not be drawn in the regular monthly pay bill of that period, are drawn by the establishment through:

options.A: A supplementary pay bill prepared for the purpose
options.B: The travelling allowance bill of the railway servant
options.C: The contingent bill of the office
options.D: A fresh appointment order issued by the competent authority

e: Arrears of pay and allowances that could not be drawn in the regular monthly pay bill are drawn through a supplementary pay bill prepared for the purpose, supported by the due-drawn statement.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 9 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 63,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at twelve times the emoluments as admissible for this length of service, will be:
e: For death with 5 to 11 years of service, the death gratuity slab is 12 times emoluments. Here service is 9 years, so gratuity = 12 x Rs 63,000 = Rs 7,56,000.

q: In regard to a privilege pass issued to a railway servant under the Railway Pass Rules, the correct position is that the pass:

options.A: Is not transferable, and is valid only for the persons whose names are endorsed on it
options.B: Can be transferred by the railway servant to any member of his family by an endorsement on it
options.C: Can be sold by the railway servant to another railway servant of the same station
options.D: Can be used by any person who produces it at the time of travel

e: Under the Railway Pass Rules, a privilege pass is not transferable and is valid only for the persons whose names are endorsed on it; use by any other person is irregular.

q: The statement which accompanies a supplementary (arrear) pay bill, setting out in respect of each railway servant the amount of pay and allowances due to him, the amount already drawn by him and the net amount now claimed, is known as the:

options.A: Absentee statement
options.B: Increment certificate
options.C: Last Pay Certificate
options.D: Due-drawn statement

e: The statement accompanying a supplementary arrear pay bill, showing for each railway servant the amount due, the amount already drawn and the net amount now claimed, is the due-drawn statement.

q: On the grant of a financial upgradation under the Modified Assured Career Progression scheme to a railway servant, if he is thereafter regularly promoted to a post in the same pay level as that of the financial upgradation already granted to him, the position regarding fixation of his pay on such promotion is that:

options.A: He is granted one more increment by way of fixation benefit on the promotion
options.B: No fixation benefit of an increment is admissible to him again, as his pay already stands fixed in that very level
options.C: His pay is refixed at the minimum of the level on the promotion
options.D: He is granted two increments on the promotion in lieu of the earlier upgradation

e: Under MACPS pay fixation rules, if a railway servant is regularly promoted to a post in the same pay level as the financial upgradation already granted, no further fixation benefit of an increment is admissible, as his pay already stands fixed in that level.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering only 1 year of qualifying service and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 59,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Service gratuity is half a month's emoluments per completed six-monthly period. 1 year = 2 periods, so 2 x Rs 29,500 = Rs 59,000.

q: The pay of a gazetted railway servant is drawn by the establishment on the basis of the pay slip issued for the purpose by:

options.A: The Accounts Office, which issues the pay slip showing the pay and allowances admissible to the officer
options.B: The Railway Recruitment Board
options.C: The recognised officers' association of the Railway
options.D: The gazetted railway servant himself, by a self-declaration

e: The pay of a gazetted railway servant is drawn on the basis of the pay slip issued by the Accounts Office, showing the pay and allowances admissible to the officer; it is not drawn on self-declaration.

q: A claim for arrears of pay and allowances of a railway servant, which has not been preferred within one year of the date on which it became due, can be paid only after it has been subjected to:

options.A: A vigilance inquiry conducted by the Vigilance Department
options.B: Pre-audit by the Accounts Office, in accordance with the rules for investigation of arrear claims
options.C: The approval of the Railway Board in every case
options.D: An inquiry by the Central Administrative Tribunal

e: Under the rules for investigation of arrear claims, a claim for arrears of pay and allowances not preferred within one year of becoming due can be paid only after pre-audit by the Accounts Office.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 21 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 47,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: For death after 20 years, death gratuity is half a month's emoluments per completed six-monthly period, capped at 33 times emoluments. 21 years = 42 periods, so 42 x Rs 23,500 = Rs 9,87,000, within the cap of Rs 15,51,000.

q: A candidate, or a railway servant, who has been declared medically unfit for railway service on a medical examination may prefer an appeal against the medical findings, whereupon a re-examination is arranged, in accordance with the prescribed procedure, by:

options.A: A medical board, the matter being dealt with at the level of the Chief Medical Director of the Railway
options.B: The General Manager of the Railway personally
options.C: The Railway Recruitment Board which selected the candidate
options.D: A private medical practitioner chosen by the candidate himself

e: An appeal against medical unfitness is dealt with at the level of the Chief Medical Director of the Railway, and re-examination is arranged by a medical board in accordance with the prescribed procedure in IREM.

q: Under the National Pension System, a subscriber who has attained the age of 60 years may, instead of finally exiting from the system at that age, elect to:

options.A: Transfer his entire accumulated pension wealth to his Tier-II account
options.B: Withdraw the entire amount in cash in all cases, without purchasing any annuity
options.C: Convert his account into a General Provident Fund account of the Railways
options.D: Continue to keep his Tier-I account in operation, or defer the withdrawal of the lump sum and the purchase of annuity, up to the age of 85 years

e: An NPS subscriber may now continue the account up to the age of 85 years. (Source: PFRDA (Exits and Withdrawals under NPS) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025, notified 16.12.2025; PIB Release ID 2206763 dated 19.12.2025.)

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 11 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 39,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per completed six-monthly period. 11 years = 22 periods, so 22 x Rs 9,750 (one-fourth of Rs 39,000) = Rs 2,14,500.

q: A 'Duty Card Pass' on the Railways is issued to:

options.A: A railway servant whose duties require him to travel frequently within a specified jurisdiction, so that he can travel on duty without obtaining a separate duty pass for each journey
options.B: Every retired railway servant for travel to his place of settlement
options.C: The family members of a railway servant for travel during his leave
options.D: A railway servant for conveying his personal effects on transfer

e: A Duty Card Pass is issued to a railway servant whose duties require frequent travel within a specified jurisdiction, so that he can travel on duty without obtaining a separate duty pass for each journey.

q: Family pension received by the widow of a deceased railway servant is chargeable to income-tax in her hands under the head:

options.A: Income from salaries
options.B: Income from house property
options.C: Income from other sources
options.D: It is wholly exempt from income-tax in all cases

e: Family pension received by the widow of a deceased railway servant is taxed in her hands under the head Income from other sources, as she receives it as a family member and not as an employee under a contract of service.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 81,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate, at 30 per cent of the last basic pay drawn, will be:

options.A: Rs 40,500 per month
options.B: Rs 24,300 per month
options.C: Rs 16,200 per month
options.D: Rs 27,000 per month

e: Normal rate family pension is 30 per cent of last basic pay. 30 per cent of Rs 81,000 = Rs 24,300 per month.

q: An ex-serviceman who has already secured employment in a civil service or post under the Government by availing of the benefit of reservation for ex-servicemen is:

options.A: Not entitled to avail of the benefit of reservation for ex-servicemen again for securing another civil employment
options.B: Entitled to avail of the reservation benefit again for every subsequent post
options.C: Entitled to the reservation benefit twice in his lifetime
options.D: Entitled to the reservation benefit again after a gap of five years

e: Under the ex-servicemen reservation instructions, the benefit can be availed only once for securing civil employment; once used to get a Government post, it cannot be claimed again for another civil post.

q: Fixed Medical Allowance is admissible to a railway pensioner who is not availing the outdoor treatment facility under the railway health scheme and who resides at a place situated beyond the following distance from the nearest railway hospital or health unit:

options.A: 1 kilometre
options.B: 5 kilometres
options.C: 10 kilometres
options.D: 2.5 kilometres

e: Fixed Medical Allowance under the railway health scheme is payable to a pensioner not availing outdoor treatment only if his residence is beyond 2.5 kilometres from the nearest railway hospital or health unit.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 150 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 66,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him will be:
e: Leave encashment is (pay + DA) x days / 30: (Rs 66,000 + 50 percent DA Rs 33,000) = Rs 99,000; Rs 99,000 / 30 x 150 days = Rs 4,95,000, under RS (Pension) Rules on Leave on Average Pay at credit.

q: Gold metal passes on the Railways are issued to:

options.A: All gazetted railway officers of Group 'A' and Group 'B'
options.B: All officers in the Higher Administrative Grade and Senior Administrative Grade
options.C: Divisional Railway Managers of all divisions
options.D: The Chairman and the Members of the Railway Board

e: Under the railway pass rules, Gold metal passes are the highest category and are issued only to the Chairman and the Members of the Railway Board.

q: The number of holidays, including the three National Holidays, ordinarily admissible in a calendar year to the staff of railway administrative offices, as per the list of closed holidays, is:
e: Administrative offices on the Railways ordinarily observe 17 closed holidays in a calendar year, including the 3 National Holidays, as per the approved list of holidays.

q: The findings of a Departmental Promotion Committee in respect of a railway servant were kept in a sealed cover on account of disciplinary proceedings pending against him. On the conclusion of the proceedings, he is completely exonerated of the charges. In such a case, he is:

options.A: Promoted with effect from the date on which his immediate junior was promoted on the basis of the same proceedings of the Committee, with the consequential benefits
options.B: Considered afresh for promotion only against a future vacancy
options.C: Promoted only from the date of his exoneration, without any retrospective effect
options.D: Denied promotion altogether, as his case was once kept in a sealed cover

e: Under the sealed cover procedure, on complete exoneration the DPC recommendation is given effect from the date his immediate junior was promoted on the same DPC proceedings, with consequential benefits.

q: A railway servant who is undergoing a penalty imposed on him in disciplinary proceedings is, during the currency of that penalty:

options.A: Considered for promotion in the normal course, the penalty having no effect on his promotion
options.B: Permanently debarred from promotion even after the penalty expires
options.C: Considered for promotion only on the recommendation of his trade union
options.D: Not considered for promotion to a higher post during the period of currency of the penalty

e: During the currency of a penalty imposed in disciplinary proceedings, the railway servant is not considered for promotion to a higher post; consideration resumes only after the penalty expires.

q: The 'consequential seniority' admissible to railway servants belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes on their promotion by reservation flows from the provision contained in the Constitution in:

options.A: Article 16(4A), as amended by the Constitution (Eighty-fifth Amendment) Act
options.B: Article 16(4B)
options.C: Article 335
options.D: Article 46

e: Consequential seniority for SC and ST promotees flows from Article 16(4A) of the Constitution, as amended by the Constitution (Eighty-fifth Amendment) Act, 2001.

q: Reservation of 4 per cent for persons with benchmark disabilities in direct recruitment on the Railways is distributed among the specified categories of disability in the manner that:

options.A: The entire 4 per cent is reserved for locomotor disability alone
options.B: 2 per cent is reserved for visual disability and 2 per cent for hearing disability
options.C: 1 per cent is reserved for the blind and low-vision category, 1 per cent for the deaf and hard-of-hearing category, 1 per cent for locomotor disability, and 1 per cent for the remaining specified disabilities, including autism, intellectual disability and multiple disabilities
options.D: The 4 per cent is distributed equally among all the zonal Railways

e: The 4 percent reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities is split 1 percent each for blind and low vision, deaf and hard of hearing, locomotor disability, and the remaining specified disabilities including autism, intellectual disability and multiple disabilities.

q: For the purpose of reservation for Other Backward Classes in direct recruitment, a candidate falls in the 'creamy layer', and is thus excluded from the benefit of reservation, where:

options.A: His parents' annual income from salary alone exceeds Rs 8 lakh
options.B: Both his parents are Group 'A' (Class I) officers, by virtue of the status held by them, irrespective of the income test
options.C: He himself is employed in a Group 'C' post
options.D: His father is employed in a public sector undertaking in any capacity

e: Under the OBC creamy layer criteria, a candidate is excluded on status alone where both parents are Group A (Class I) officers, irrespective of the income test.

q: 'Nivaran', the online facility provided on the Railways, is meant for:

options.A: The booking of retiring rooms by railway passengers
options.B: The submission of income-tax returns by railway servants
options.C: The allotment of railway quarters to serving staff
options.D: The redressal of the grievances of serving railway employees, who can lodge and track their grievances online

e: Nivaran is the online grievance redressal portal on the Railways on which serving railway employees can lodge and track their grievances.

q: Railway servants who are entrusted with the handling of cash and stores in the course of their duties, such as cashiers and pay clerks, are required, in accordance with the prescribed rules, to:

options.A: Deposit one month's pay with the Railway Board as a donation
options.B: Execute a personal bond undertaking to retire on demand
options.C: Furnish security deposit, or execute a fidelity guarantee bond, of the prescribed amount, as security for the faithful discharge of their duties
options.D: Obtain a licence from the State Government for handling cash

e: Staff entrusted with cash and stores, such as cashiers and pay clerks, must furnish a security deposit or execute a fidelity guarantee bond of the prescribed amount under IREM for faithful discharge of their duties.

q: Recruitment on the Railways against the sports quota is made on the basis of:

options.A: Trials conducted by a Trial Committee and the assessment of the sports achievements and educational qualifications of the candidates, without a written examination
options.B: The normal written examination conducted by the Railway Recruitment Board
options.C: Nomination by the Railway Sports Promotion Board alone
options.D: Seniority in the waiting list of the Employment Exchange

e: Sports quota recruitment is made without a written examination, on the basis of trials by a Trial Committee and assessment of sports achievements and educational qualifications.

q: Where a railway servant remains absent from duty without authorisation for a continuous period exceeding five years, the position under the leave rules is that he is:

options.A: Granted Extra Ordinary Leave for the entire period automatically
options.B: Deemed to have resigned from railway service, unless the competent authority, in view of the circumstances of the case, determines otherwise
options.C: Treated as having retired voluntarily from service
options.D: Placed under suspension for the entire period of his absence

e: Under the leave rules in IREM, unauthorised absence exceeding five years continuously is treated as deemed resignation, unless the competent authority determines otherwise in the circumstances of the case.

q: A railway pensioner who has applied for commutation of a portion of his pension may withdraw his application by giving a written notice to the Head of Office, provided the withdrawal is sought:

options.A: At any time, even after the commuted value has been paid to him
options.B: Within one year of the payment of the commuted value
options.C: Only with the prior approval of the Railway Board
options.D: Before the commutation becomes absolute

e: Under the RS (Pension) Rules on commutation, the applicant may withdraw the commutation application by written notice to the Head of Office at any time before the commutation becomes absolute.

q: A transfer on mutual exchange between two railway servants can be ordered only where the two railway servants:

options.A: Belong to different categories and different grades
options.B: Have both completed less than two years of service
options.C: Are both working in the same division of the same Railway
options.D: Belong to the same category and grade and have both been appointed through the same mode of recruitment, that is, both are direct recruits or both are promotees

e: Mutual exchange transfer requires both railway servants to be in the same category and grade and to have been appointed through the same mode of recruitment, both direct recruits or both promotees.

q: Appointment on compassionate grounds on the Railways can be considered in favour of a dependent member of the family of a railway servant who:

options.A: Has retired from service on attaining the age of superannuation
options.B: Has been transferred to a distant station in public interest
options.C: Dies while in service, or is retired from service on medical invalidation, having been declared permanently incapacitated for further service
options.D: Has resigned from service to take up another employment

e: Compassionate appointment is considered only for a dependent family member of a railway servant who dies in service or is retired on medical invalidation after being declared permanently incapacitated for further service.

q: The incentive admissible to a railway servant for acquiring a fresh higher qualification, which is relevant to his duties, is payable to him in the form of:

options.A: A one-time lump sum incentive, and not as advance increments in pay
options.B: Advance increments in his pay level, recurring every year
options.C: An additional increment of pay every year for the rest of his service
options.D: Promotion to the next higher post without any selection

e: The incentive for acquiring a fresh higher qualification relevant to duties is now paid as a one-time lump sum incentive, and not as advance increments, as per Railway Board instructions.

q: A 'supernumerary post' on the Railways means:

options.A: A post sanctioned permanently as part of the regular cadre of a service
options.B: A post created over and above the sanctioned cadre strength, to accommodate the lien of a particular incumbent, which is not to be operated as a regular working post and ceases when the incumbent vacates it
options.C: A post whose pay is charged to the cost of a specific work or estimate
options.D: A post filled only by a candidate selected by the Union Public Service Commission

e: A supernumerary post is created over and above the sanctioned cadre to accommodate the lien of a particular incumbent; it is not a regular working post and ceases when the incumbent vacates it.

q: Temporary posts on the Railways, which have been in existence continuously for a prescribed long period and are likely to be required indefinitely, are required to be reviewed for being made permanent. The period of continuous existence ordinarily prescribed for this purpose is:

options.A: One year
options.B: Two years
options.C: Three years
options.D: Ten years

e: Temporary posts in continuous existence for three years and likely to be required indefinitely are required to be reviewed for conversion into permanent posts.

q: For the purpose of computing the 'average emoluments' of a railway servant for pension, where, during the last ten months of his service, he was absent on Extra Ordinary Leave granted otherwise than on medical certificate, or a period of his absence was treated as dies non, the correct position is that:

options.A: Such periods are reckoned in the ten months with full emoluments as if he had been on duty
options.B: His pension is reduced by one-half in all such cases
options.C: The entire ten months are treated as non-qualifying and his pension is denied
options.D: Such periods are excluded, and the average is worked out on the emoluments drawn during the ten months of qualifying service immediately preceding, by extending the period backwards to that extent

e: For average emoluments under the RS (Pension) Rules, periods of EOL (other than on medical certificate) or dies non in the last 10 months are excluded and the 10 months are completed by extending backwards over qualifying service.

q: Cash equivalent of leave salary, in respect of the Leave on Average Pay at the credit of a railway servant, is admissible to him where he is:

options.A: Removed from service as a measure of penalty
options.B: Dismissed from service as a measure of penalty
options.C: Compulsorily retired from service as a measure of penalty
options.D: Struck off the rolls on account of unauthorised absence

e: Cash equivalent of leave salary for LAP at credit is admissible on compulsory retirement as a penalty, but is denied on dismissal or removal from service and on being struck off for unauthorised absence.

q: Where a railway servant is permanently absorbed in a public sector undertaking or an autonomous body, with the consent of the Railways and in public interest, the absorption is treated, for the purpose of his pensionary benefits for the railway service rendered by him, as:

options.A: A resignation simpliciter, entailing forfeiture of his past service
options.B: His retirement from railway service, on the basis of which pro-rata pensionary benefits are admissible to him
options.C: A transfer on deputation for an indefinite period
options.D: A break in his service for all purposes

e: Permanent absorption in a PSU or autonomous body with consent and in public interest is treated as retirement from railway service, so pro-rata pensionary benefits for the railway service are admissible.

q: Where a railway servant dies while he is under suspension, before the disciplinary proceedings instituted against him are concluded, the period of his suspension is, for the purpose of the family pension and gratuity payable to his family, treated as:

options.A: A period of absence not counting for any benefit
options.B: A period treated as dies non
options.C: A period spent on duty for all purposes
options.D: A period of Extra Ordinary Leave without pay

e: If a railway servant dies under suspension before proceedings conclude, the suspension period is treated as spent on duty for all purposes for family pension and gratuity under the RS (Pension) Rules.

q: Where the amount at the credit of a retired railway servant in the General Provident Fund is not withdrawn by him immediately on his retirement, interest on the amount continues to be admissible to him, without any special sanction, for a period of up to:

options.A: Three months after his retirement
options.B: Six months after the month in which the amount became payable on his retirement
options.C: Two years after his retirement
options.D: Five years after his retirement

e: Interest on the GPF balance of a retired railway servant continues without special sanction for up to six months after the month in which the amount became payable on retirement.

q: In regard to the utilisation of House Building Advance for the repayment of a housing loan taken earlier from another source, the correct position is that the advance:

options.A: Can never be utilised for repayment of any earlier loan
options.B: Can be utilised for repayment of a housing loan already taken by the railway servant from a recognised bank or housing finance institution for the purchase or construction of his house, subject to the prescribed conditions
options.C: Can be utilised only for repayment of a loan taken from a private moneylender
options.D: Can be utilised for repayment of a housing loan only after the railway servant has retired from service

e: House Building Advance may be used to repay a housing loan earlier taken from a recognised bank or housing finance institution for purchase or construction of the house, subject to the prescribed conditions.

q: Under the 'check-off' facility available on the Railways, a railway servant can authorise in writing the recovery from his salary, and its remittance to his trade union, of:

options.A: His Provident Fund subscription
options.B: The donations payable by him to a political party
options.C: The court attachment dues recoverable from him
options.D: His membership subscription to a recognised trade union of which he is a member

e: Under the check-off facility, a railway servant may authorise in writing recovery of his membership subscription to a recognised trade union from his salary and its remittance to that union.

q: On the retirement of a railway servant, a 'settlement pass' is issued to enable:

options.A: The railway servant and the members of his family to travel to his home town or other selected place of settlement
options.B: The railway servant to travel on duty to the station from which he retired
options.C: The Accounts Office to settle his pension papers at his home station
options.D: The family of the railway servant to travel on privilege account every year after his retirement

e: A settlement pass is issued on retirement to enable the railway servant and his family to travel to his home town or the selected place of settlement.

q: Post-retirement complimentary passes admissible to the widow of a deceased retired railway servant cease to be issued to her on:

options.A: Her attaining the age of 60 years
options.B: Her remarriage
options.C: Her taking up any private employment
options.D: The expiry of ten years from the death of the railway servant

e: Post-retirement complimentary passes to the widow of a deceased retired railway servant cease on her remarriage.

q: A dispute or doubt regarding the classification of an employment under the Hours of Employment Regulations, that is, whether it is 'Intensive', 'Continuous', 'Essentially Intermittent' or 'Excluded', is decided by:

options.A: The General Manager of the zonal Railway
options.B: The Divisional Railway Manager of the division concerned
options.C: The Regional Labour Commissioner, whose decision in the matter is binding
options.D: The recognised federation of railway employees of the Railway

e: A dispute or doubt on classification of employment under the Hours of Employment Regulations is decided by the Regional Labour Commissioner, whose decision is binding.

q: Under Section 27 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, the power to make rules, by notification in the Official Gazette, to carry out the provisions of the Act generally vests in:

options.A: The Central Information Commission
options.B: The First Appellate Authority
options.C: The Chief Justice of India
options.D: The appropriate Government

e: Section 27 of the RTI Act, 2005 vests the power to make rules to carry out the Act generally, by notification in the Official Gazette, in the appropriate Government.

q: Under Section 12 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, notice of the situation of the registered office of a registered trade union of railway servants, and of every change in the situation of that office, is required to be given to:

options.A: The Registrar of Trade Unions, who shall record the same in the register maintained by him
options.B: The Labour Commissioner of the State
options.C: The employer of the members of the trade union
options.D: The District Magistrate of the district

e: Section 12 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 requires notice of the situation of the registered office of a registered trade union, and of every change, to be given to the Registrar of Trade Unions for recording.

q: Under Section 17 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, the report of a Board or Court, and the award of a Labour Court, an Industrial Tribunal or a National Tribunal, are required to be published by the appropriate Government within the following period from the date of their receipt by it:

options.A: Seven days
options.B: Fifteen days
options.C: Sixty days
options.D: Thirty days

e: Section 17 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 requires the appropriate Government to publish the report of a Board or Court and the award of a Labour Court, Tribunal or National Tribunal within thirty days of receipt.

q: Under Section 14 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, for the purpose of computing the number of days on which an employee has worked in an establishment in an accounting year, he shall be deemed to have worked on the days on which he has:

options.A: Been laid off, been on leave with salary or wages, been absent due to temporary disablement caused by an employment injury, or been on maternity leave with salary or wages
options.B: Remained absent without leave for any reason whatsoever
options.C: Participated in a strike declared illegal under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
options.D: Remained absent on account of his detention in police custody in a criminal case

e: Section 14 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 deems an employee to have worked on days of lay-off, leave with salary or wages, absence due to temporary disablement from employment injury, and maternity leave with salary or wages.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 5 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 43,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at twelve times the emoluments as admissible for this length of service, will be:
e: Death gratuity for 5 to 11 years of service is 12x emoluments under the RS (Pension) Rules: 12 x Rs 43,000 = Rs 5,16,000.

q: Under Section 3 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the controlling authority for the administration of the Act is appointed by:

options.A: The employer of the establishment concerned
options.B: The Employees' Provident Fund Commissioner
options.C: The appropriate Government, by notification, which may appoint different controlling authorities for different areas or classes of employees
options.D: The District Collector, by a general order

e: Section 3 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 provides that the controlling authority is appointed by the appropriate Government by notification, which may appoint different authorities for different areas or classes of employees.

q: Under Section 7 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where half-monthly payments are payable to an employee for temporary disablement, the Commissioner may, on the application of the employer or of the employee, order the commutation of the half-monthly payments for a lump sum amount, provided the payments have been continued during a period of not less than:

options.A: Three months
options.B: Six months
options.C: Twelve months
options.D: One month

e: Section 7 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 permits commutation of half-monthly payments for temporary disablement into a lump sum only where the payments have continued for not less than six months.

q: Under Section 7 of the Apprentices Act, 1961, the contract of apprenticeship of an Act Apprentice engaged in a railway workshop may be terminated by:

options.A: The employer at his sole discretion, without any order of any authority
options.B: The Inspector of Factories of the area
options.C: The Apprenticeship Adviser, if he is satisfied, on an application made by either party to the contract, that a party has failed to carry out the terms and conditions of the contract or that it is otherwise expedient to terminate it
options.D: The Registrar of Trade Unions

e: Section 7 of the Apprentices Act, 1961 allows termination of an apprenticeship contract only by the Apprenticeship Adviser, on application by either party, if a party has failed to carry out the contract terms or it is otherwise expedient.

q: Under Section 6 of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, a Local Complaints Committee is constituted by the District Officer to receive complaints of sexual harassment from establishments:

options.A: Where the Internal Complaints Committee has not been constituted due to the workplace having less than ten workers, or where the complaint is against the employer himself
options.B: Only where the workplace is situated in a rural area
options.C: Only where no woman is employed at the workplace
options.D: Where the Internal Complaints Committee has failed to dispose of a complaint within ninety days

e: Section 6 of the POSH Act, 2013 requires a Local Complaints Committee where the Internal Complaints Committee has not been constituted because the workplace has less than ten workers, or where the complaint is against the employer himself.

q: Under Section 17 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, in respect of contempt of the Central Administrative Tribunal itself, the Tribunal has and exercises:

options.A: No power to punish for contempt in any case
options.B: The same jurisdiction, powers and authority as a High Court has in respect of contempt of itself
options.C: Only the power to report the matter to the High Court for action
options.D: The powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure only

e: Section 17 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 gives the Tribunal, for contempt of itself, the same jurisdiction, powers and authority as a High Court has for contempt of itself.

q: Under Section 11 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, the minimum rates of wages fixed under the Act shall be paid:

options.A: Wholly in kind, in every case
options.B: Partly in cash and partly in kind, in every case
options.C: In cash; payment in kind is permissible only where it has been the custom to pay wages wholly or partly in kind and the appropriate Government has, by notification, authorised such payment
options.D: In the manner decided by the employer at his discretion

e: Section 11 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 requires minimum wages to be paid in cash; payment in kind is allowed only where it has been the custom and the appropriate Government has authorised it by notification.

q: Under Section 7 of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, every principal employer of an establishment to which the Act applies is required to make an application for the registration of the establishment to:

options.A: The licensing officer appointed under the Act
options.B: The registering officer appointed under the Act, in the prescribed manner and within the prescribed period
options.C: The Inspector appointed under the Factories Act, 1948
options.D: The Registrar of Trade Unions

e: Section 7 of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 requires every principal employer to apply for registration of the establishment to the registering officer in the prescribed manner and period.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 24 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 53,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Death gratuity for 20 years or more is half a month emoluments per six-monthly period, capped at 33x: 24 years = 48 periods x Rs 26,500 = Rs 12,72,000, which is below the cap of Rs 17,49,000.

q: Under Section 28 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, in respect of matters such as the fee payable for obtaining information, also vests in:

options.A: The competent authority, as defined in the Act, by notification in the Official Gazette
options.B: The State Information Commission in every case
options.C: The Central Public Information Officer
options.D: The Appellate Authority under the Act

e: Section 28 of the RTI Act, 2005 vests rule-making power on matters such as the fee for obtaining information in the competent authority, by notification in the Official Gazette.

q: Under Section 21A of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, a person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, an office-bearer of a registered trade union of railway servants if:

options.A: He is not a graduate
options.B: He has not been a member of the trade union for at least five years
options.C: He has been convicted by a court of an offence involving moral turpitude and sentenced to imprisonment, unless a period of five years has elapsed since his release
options.D: He is employed in a supervisory capacity in the establishment

e: Section 21A of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 disqualifies a person convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude and sentenced to imprisonment from being an office-bearer, unless five years have elapsed since his release.

q: Under Section 19(3) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, an award of a Labour Court, an Industrial Tribunal or a National Tribunal shall, subject to the provisions of the Act, remain in operation for the following period from the date on which the award becomes enforceable:

options.A: Six months
options.B: One year
options.C: Three years
options.D: Five years

e: Section 19(3) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 provides that an award remains in operation for one year from the date it becomes enforceable, subject to the provisions of the Act.

q: Under Section 17 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, where in any accounting year an employer has paid any customary bonus or interim bonus to an employee, the position is that:

options.A: The amount so paid cannot be adjusted against the bonus payable under the Act in any case
options.B: The employee shall refund the whole of the amount so paid before claiming bonus under the Act
options.C: The employer is entitled to deduct the amount so paid from the amount of bonus payable to the employee under the Act for that accounting year, and the employee shall be entitled only to the balance, if any
options.D: The amount so paid is treated as a loan recoverable from the wages of the employee

e: Section 17 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 entitles the employer to deduct any customary or interim bonus already paid from the bonus payable under the Act for that accounting year, the employee getting only the balance.

q: Under Section 4A of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, relating to compulsory insurance, every employer, other than an employer of an establishment belonging to or under the control of the Central Government or a State Government, is required to:

options.A: Obtain insurance, in the prescribed manner, from the Life Insurance Corporation of India or any other prescribed insurer, for his liability for payment towards gratuity under the Act, or establish an approved gratuity fund
options.B: Deposit the whole gratuity amount of all employees with the controlling authority in advance
options.C: Obtain a bank guarantee from the Reserve Bank of India for the gratuity liability
options.D: Insure every employee under the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme only

e: Section 4A of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 requires every non-Government employer to obtain insurance from LIC or a prescribed insurer for gratuity liability, or establish an approved gratuity fund.

q: Under Section 13 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where an employer has paid compensation to an employee for an injury caused under such circumstances as create a legal liability in some person other than the employer to pay damages in respect thereof, the employer is entitled to:

options.A: Recover the compensation from the wages of the employee
options.B: Be indemnified by the person so liable to pay damages
options.C: Recover the compensation from the Commissioner for employees' compensation
options.D: Nothing, as the payment of compensation extinguishes all further claims

e: Section 13 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 entitles an employer who has paid compensation for an injury creating legal liability in a third person to be indemnified by that person.

q: Under Section 11 of the Apprentices Act, 1961, in regard to the obligations of an employer who has engaged Act Apprentices in a railway workshop, the correct position is that the employer shall:

options.A: Provide the facilities required for imparting practical training to the apprentices in the designated trades, in accordance with the prescribed programme and syllabus
options.B: Pay to every apprentice wages equal to those of a regular worker of the same trade
options.C: Absorb every apprentice in regular employment on the completion of his training
options.D: Recover the cost of the training from the apprentices in monthly instalments

e: Section 11 of the Apprentices Act, 1961 obliges the employer to provide the facilities required for imparting practical training to apprentices in the designated trades as per the prescribed programme and syllabus.
